recentItems.title: US-mediated talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war begin in Abu Dhabi
recentItems.description:
Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday, as Washington made another push to end the war that followed Moscow's all-out invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago. This is the first such meeting since February.

recentItems.title: WATCH: US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine begin in Abu Dhabi
recentItems.description:
Watch as three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States open in Abu Dhabi in in the United Arab Emirates. Jared Kushner, who along with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff is trying to broker a settlement, said he believed there were “some good ideas how to bridge” the differences between the two sides. recentItems.title: Exclusive: AP joins the EU naval patrol fighting piracy in the Gulf of Aden
recentItems.description:
Piracy fears are rising in the Gulf of Aden as conflicts across the Middle East and Horn of Africa threaten stability along one of the world's busiest shipping routes. The Associated Press joined the Spanish frigate Santa Maria on a patrol with the European Union's Operation Atalanta, an anti-piracy mission, as naval commanders warned that regional instability could fuel a fresh surge in pirate activity. More than 70 incidents have been reported since November 2023, with roughly half occurring in 2026. (AP video by Sam McNeil)

recentItems.title: NAACP says no legal issues in Mississippi as vote count continues in close Senate race
recentItems.description:
NAACP officials said there have been no major legal issues as the deadline for voters to cast affidavit ballots draws near. Officials also lauded the progress they've made in a Republican stronghold, harkening back to the Civil Rights era and imagining more progress to come.  (AP Video by Sophie Bates)

recentItems.title: Timeline: How did Nvidia's CEO get caught up in an alleged spy plot?
recentItems.description: President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent. The sudden emergence of Huang’s infidelity has rocked the political class and America’s tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence. Here's a timeline of how the story has unfolded so far.
